**ACE Battle DAO Governance Whitepaper – V1-1 (July 2026\) – final draft 30-07**

**Summary**

This whitepaper describes and justifies the design of smart contract governance subsystem of ACE Battle franchise network. It describes the utility and architecture of ACE Battle tokens, their ecosystem role, ownership, tentative principles of implementation, and roadmaps. The paper references the current state and visible prospects of the project development, and is subject to future updates and revisions.  
The paper begins with a working introduction to the ACE Battle economy. As the economy aims for community-driven governance of financial flows and participant requirements, the blockchain tokens are suitable to represent stakes and voting power in the governing decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs) at the level of countries, regions and the world. For the fair distribution of governing power and attraction of resources, the project introduces three classes of tokens circulating within the project’s smart contract network, as well as in open markets.  
The remainder of the paper outlines the governance and smart contracts architecture of the ecosystem. It covers the three classes of ACE Battle tokens in turn, with the focus on their utility and on-chain flows. 

**ACE Battle economy overview**

ACE Battle is the sports and gaming franchise brand and decentralized Web3 ecosystem for amateur runners. The reader is referred to the dedicated project documents for a comprehensive description of the branded sports game, participation models, and full coverage of the DAOs competence on all levels. This overview introduces the concepts relevant to the project’s on-chain governance.  
The sports events are organized by local commercial franchisee companies, processing their revenues via a single independent worldwide IT and payment infrastructure operator (IT Operator). The Operator splits the event revenues according to a pre-determined percentage distribution, with 85% available to the franchisee, and the rest distributed for ecosystem needs. In particular, the event participants compete for a rewards pool comprising 5% of revenue. Ecosystem participants (known as “Enthusiasts”) are required to make seasonal payments and lock a security deposit to safeguard against misbehavior, which constitutes an “engage-to-earn” model, including but not limited to sports activities.  
The remainder of the revenue distribution, excluding the corporate administrative costs, is managed by the community. Brand promotion, marketing, infrastructural development, training and referee work is delegated to the single country-level or region-level Federation of sport clubs. The seasonal budgets of the Federation is approved and effectively financed from a dedicated treasury by the country/regional DAO consisting of the region-level governance token holders (denoted as the ACE\[cc\] token class). The Federation is not engaged with the on-chain infrastructure directly; instead, it receives the fiat costs from the IT Operator as ordered by the DAO and financially backed by the DAO-approved treasury. The regional DAO further approves the country-level requirements for participants’ payments and deposits, and is fully responsible for financial management of the DAO treasury. The latter is replenished according to the revenue split percentage by the IT Operator.  
The global DAO, consisting of the global governance (ACEG) token holders, orders the IT Operator to process the Federations budget payments, makes decisions as to the new regions establishment, additional funding of the regional treasuries, and management of the global treasury, financed via the same revenue distribution.

**Governance and smart contracts architecture**

This section describes the utility and on-chain architecture of three token classes present in the ACE Battle ecosystem:

1) ACER, the internal fiat-denominated technical representation of on-chain value;  
2) ACE\[cc\], the class of governance tokens for the country/regional DAOs;  
3) ACEG, the global DAO governance token. 

	ACER

The ACER token acts as a stable fiat-denominated internal representation of value and an intermediary asset for internal marketplaces. While its ownership is open to the ACE Battle ecosystem participants subject to KYC, its on-chain circulation is restricted to the whitelisted holders, their associated wallets and contracts. Due to this, ACER is not a stablecoin and can not be used for on-chain payments for products and services.  
The token is managed by two partially overlapping categories of subjects, owners and whitelisted holders. The holders may (and in certain cases required to) act on behalf of the owners as their technical representatives.  
Thanks to its software implementation, the token may have additional protection against malicious attacks.

		Token role

			Internal representation of value

The ACER token represents the monetary value attracted to the ACE Battle ecosystem and is fully backed by fiat resources and stablecoin treasuries managed by the IT Operator. The token’s main purpose is to aggregate different value storage media in the on-chain infrastructure.  
The holders may on behalf of the represented owners make requests to the IT Operator to convert the ACER stock to fiat or on-chain stablecoins at the 1:1 ratio without restrictions, the Operator being responsible for exchange and fiat/stablecoin transfers to the owner.  
The management processes by the Operator for off-chain and on-chain exchange of ACER are to be determined.

			Inter-pool transfers

The ACER token is used as the paired crypto asset in the internal automated market making pools. The whitelisted holders manage their own ACER stock or custody by operating treasury smart contracts, managing liquidity of the internal pools, and performing inter-pool and inter-treasury transfers.   

		Token ownership

			Owners

The ACER tokens will in part be owned by the global Orphan DAO, acting as the whitelisted holder on its own behalf, which can be disallowed by its charter to convert its owned stock to fiat or stablecoins. Other owners will include natural and legal persons participating in the ecosystem and technically represented by the IT Operator. Their ownership will be managed as the off-chain custodial accounts.

Whitelisted holders

Whitelisted holders may possess ACER tokens in their external wallets or accessed smart contracts. They will be exclusively limited to: 1\) the IT Operator, representing the owners of the off-chain custodial accounts, 2\) the country and regional DAOs, acting as a partial representative of the global Orphan DAO regarding ACER ownership, 3\) the Orphan DAO acting on its own behalf.

		Implementation

			Token

To avoid classification as a non-licensed stablecoin (which would be the case for non-whitelisted private circulation) and provide additional security, ACER token should be implemented according to an extended standard to be determined (e.g. ERC-1400; ERC-3643). The contract shall include the hard-coded whitelist of holders. Upgradeability of the token contract will be considered due to future inclusion of new whitelisted holders (i.e. new country/regional DAOs). As an alternative, internal swaps of the current ACER token to a new version are feasible due to restricted circulation, once the whitelist slots of the previous contract are exhausted. 

			Treasuries and vaults

The treasury smart contracts will hold the ACER stock subject to the DAO control and may be technically operated by the IT Operator at the earliest stages.  
The vaults controlled by IT Operator may be implemented as multi-signature cold wallets or contracts, depending on business processes and comparative security. 

		Roadmap

The off-chain custodial ownership of future ACER tokens for ecosystem participants will be available at project launch. The milestones include: 

1) availability of the fiat conversion for the off-chain owners by the IT Operator,  
2) deployment of the first (optionally non-whitelisted prior to ACEG internal pool launch) token contract version,  
3) transition to the extended token standard via upgrades or swaps,  
4) launch of the ACEG internal pool against the whitelisted ACER;  
5) holders’ whitelist maintenance by the IT Operator and Orphan DAO.  

	ACE\[cc\]

The country/regional governance tokens will have technically restricted circulation, but will be traded on the internal marketplace openly accessible to ecosystem participants.  
ACE\[cc\] token ownership is always mediated. Retail owners keep their stock in custody with the IT Operator; regional DAO treasuries and ACEG meta-voting treasury operate on-chain subject to voting control and operation rules.  
The newly deployed ACE\[cc\] tokens initially provide direct regional voting power to the global Orphan DAO, with a gradual transfer of the tokens to the global DAO treasury without regional voting power, subject to further global DAO voting. Later, they are repurchased into the global meta-voting treasury for increased representation of global supporters.

		Token role

			Individual security deposit

All ecosystem participants, subject to KYC, are required to make an individual security deposit in ACE\[cc\] to safeguard against potential misbehavior. This deposit may be lost wholly or in part via fines, requiring refunding in this case. It has a lock-up period of one year and is freed afterwards. The size of the deposit is voted by the country/regional DAO. The security deposit is staked off-chain and technically maintained by the IT Operator on behalf of the owner. The early withdrawal of the security deposit results in a fine that should offset the potential market appreciation since the start of the lock-up period. The fine is transferred to the regional DAO treasury.

Federation budget

Activity of the country/regional Federation is financed by selling a volume of ACE\[cc\] tokens, determined by the DAO voting, from the regional DAO treasury on the internal marketplace, and transferring the corresponding ACER revenue to the IT Operator to be exchanged for fiat due to the Federation. The DAO voting is two-staged, with the budget volume requiring approval by regional DAO and the procedural order to process the payment from the global DAO. Having control over its treasury funded by the ACE Battle ecosystem, the DAO effectively finances the Federation via mediation of ACER and ACE\[cc\], with no tokens directly available to the Federation NGO.

			Regional DAO voting stake

The ecosystem participants are able to hold the ACE\[cc\] as the voting stake in the country/regional DAO to approve the Federation budgets, establish the amount of seasonal fees and individual security deposits, and deliberate upon internal liquidity management. The stake volume is optional and partially determines the participant’s voting weight alongside the DAO security deposit described below; this is necessary for the proper operation of ACEG meta-voting treasury and during establishment of the new regions. The lock-up period for the voting stake is shorter compared to security deposits, and early withdrawal results in a fine similar to the individual deposits, transferred to the regional DAO treasury. The regional DAO voting stake is regionally restricted. The ACEG meta-voting is the only way of trans-regional governance participation.

			Regional DAO security deposit

A separate security deposit of arbitrary volume in ACE\[cc\] is required, in addition to the voting stake, to participate in the regional DAO voting. The security deposit partially determines the participant’s voting weight in the DAO; the total deposit volume limits the volume of the Federation budget approval described above. Both of these features are necessary to prevent diversion of Federation budget via the voting stake hijacking; in cases of such attempts, the security deposit is slashed and transferred wholly or in part to the global DAO treasury. The early withdrawal of the security deposit is impossible; the minimum lock-up period is equal to one year, and its continuation may modify the voting weight by a multiplier. The DAO security deposits are made off-chain and maintained by the IT Provider on behalf of the participants. The regional security deposits are not regionally restricted and are required for ACEG meta-voting. The exact rules for meta-voting security deposits are to be determined; they may be automatically provided by the meta-voting vault contract in a proportion to the holdings, or managed individually by each meta-voting participant.

		Token ownership

			Personal ownership

ACE\[cc\] ownership by natural and legal persons is always mediated.  
Ecosystem participants control their security deposits and voting stake via off-chain accounts with the IT Operator, who holds the purchased token stock in custody and sells it on the owners’ behalf.  
The freshly issued ACE\[cc\] for a new region are deposited in a dedicated vault contract and are available for proportionate meta-voting to ACEG holders, otherwise being non-transferable. This stock is transferred to the global Orphan DAO treasury according to vesting rules to be further determined. 

DAO ownership

ACE\[cc\] tokens deposited in the regional DAO treasuries have no voting impact, no personalized owners, and are controlled via approval of proposals. The proposals can only concern Federation budget funding, internal purchases/sales for the purpose of treasury accumulation, and internal liquidity supply/withdrawal for treasury replenishment.

		Implementation

			Token

The ACE\[cc\] tokens should be implemented according to an extended standard (e.g. ERC-1400; ERC-3643) allowing whitelisting of owners and interacting contracts to prevent hijacking of internal liquidity pools by outsiders (i.e. entities other than the respective regional DAO and ACEG meta-voting vault). Upgradeability of the token contract is not necessary due to the whitelist being fully known at deployment. 

			Liquidity pools

The internal pools can be implemented as forks of the industry standard solutions such as Uniswap V2. Due to support of holders’ whitelists by the token contract itself, no additional security measures are needed. A transaction involving transfers of an ACE\[cc\] token to a non-whitelisted holder (e.g. a non-managing regional DAO) should result in full revert. 

			Treasuries and vaults

Due to off-chain mediated personal ownership, the IT Operator treasuries holding the DAO security deposits and voting stakes should have their corresponding voting tokens, used for on-chain DAO voting, reclaimable by the IT Operator and otherwise non-transferable.  
ACEG meta-voting treasury and early post-minting vaults should be implemented as smart contracts, with voting weights of the contained tokens computed externally in proportion to ACEG holdings rather than internally.  
Regional and global DAO treasuries may be technically managed by the IT Operator at the early stages and directly subject to DAO control later. Tokens contained therein have no voting weight.

		Roadmap

The non-transferable voting tokens representing DAO deposits and stakes will be available at launch. The internal AMM pools will at launch be used by IT Operator and possibly contain the early non-whitelisted ACE\[cc\]. The milestones include:

1) deployment of non-transferable voting ACE\[cc\] derivatives for conducting on-chain referendums;  
2) deployment of (optionally non-whitelisted) non-upgradeable ACE\[cc\] contract/contracts;  
3) operation of the AMM pools according to the DAO-approved proposals under exclusive mediation by IT Operator responsible for circulation restrictions;  
4) replacement/swap of ACE\[cc\] tokens to whitelisted versions, replacement of the official pools, transition to technically rather than managerially restricted circulation; all of this is done before the ACEG internal pool launch;  
5) launch of the ACEG internal pool;  
6) transition to full-fledged country/regional DAO management.

	ACEG

		Token role

			Supporters’ involvement

Being tradable without restrictions on the open market, ACEG serves as a sole channel for involvement of support from the general public. An internal token marketplace, alongside the open market, is accessible both to regional and global stakeholders, with the minimum order volume and/or value required for the operation. It redirects the over-the-counter token sales proceeds to regional treasuries and global vaults to finance the ecosystem activities and development.

			Global DAO voting stake

Similarly to the regional governing DAOs, the ACEG token holders constitute a global DAO responsible for creation of new regions within the ecosystem, their initial financing, final approval of Federation budgets, as well as general governance of the ecosystem’s decentralized finance. The voting weights are proportionate to personal ACEG holdings, including the tokens locked up for vesting, serving as the free voting stake. For the insiders’ locked tokens, a mandatory market dispersal mechanism will be in place during the vesting period, in order to facilitate decentralization of voting and community empowerment.

			Regional DAO meta-voting

Part of the accumulated ACEG/ACER liquidity from the internal pool can be redirected, by a decision of the global DAO, to a buyout of the regional ACE\[cc\] governance tokens, which allows the ACEG holders to participate in the proportional regional meta-voting. The ACE\[cc\] tokens thus bought out of the regional pools are stored in the global meta-voting vault. This gives the global resource-providing stakeholders better control over regional development, encourages them to further increase their representation via direct ACEG purchases, and provides positive funding feedback to rapidly growing countries and regions. The meta-voting is accessible to all externally owned ACEG wallets.

			Global DAO security deposit

For the global DAO, brand reputation risks should be managed, and emergency mechanisms for governance transition should be in place. For this purpose, making a security deposit in ACEG tokens will be required for the global DAO voting, with the deposit volume having an impact on voting weights. In case of a severe threat to brand reputation, the security deposit can be burned by joint decision of the project founders and/or other key stakeholders, effectively ceasing the voting rights of the current holders and requiring them to replenish the deposit, which in its turn facilitates redistribution of the voting rights. The security deposit will be locked up for a minimum of at least two years, with no early withdrawals possible.

			DAO reserve

The global DAO would most likely want to ensure the funding supporters’ fair representation on the regional governance level. This is achieved via accumulation of ACE\[cc\] tokens in the global meta-voting vault, open to meta-voting by ACEG holders. Such accumulation from the regional internal pools may be funded by supporters via post-launch ACEG purchases from the internal ACEG/ACER liquidity pool. To establish and operate the pool, part of the initial ACEG token supply will be temporarily locked as the DAO reserve. It includes the initial and reserve liquidity for the internal pool as well as the global DAO treasury volume. The exact economic and technical architecture of the pool is to be determined.

		Holders

The ACEG token is freely circulating and may be held by natural and legal persons. The IT Operator is prohibited from owning ACEG tokens on its own behalf, but routinely manages the technical operations as an intermediary. The insider ownership of the tokens will be gradually reduced via mandatory market dispersal to further empower the community, according to the DAO charter.

		Implementation

			Token

The token is an unrestricted implementation of ERC-20 standard. For calculation of the security deposits voting weight, the non-transferable sdACEG tokens may be issued. For custodial ownership at the early stages (i.e. prior to the launch of the index economy), the non-transferable stACEG tokens may be issued to represent the free voting/meta-voting stake and be swapped for the liquid ACEG later.

			Liquidity pools

The internal ACEG/ACER pool should be implemented as a flexible-weight constant product exchange protocol, with the exact model to be determined.  
It may be necessary to ensure access to DAO voting for the DEX liquidity providers and centralized exchange users.

			Treasuries and vaults

The custodial vault managed by IT Operator may be necessary at the early stages. It can be implemented as a cold wallet. The derivative stACEG tokens may be issued independently and do not require a smart contract functionality of the vault.  
Global DAO security deposit vault should be implemented as a smart contract allowing timed deposits (and possibly emission of the derivative sdACEG for voting purposes) and token burning ordered via a multi-signature by key stakeholders, as an emergency vetoing measure.  
Regional and global DAO treasuries may be technically managed by the IT Operator at the early stages and directly subject to DAO control later. Tokens contained therein have no voting weight.

		Roadmap

The primary ACEG function as the governance token will be available immediately and not restricted by the vesting schedule.   
It is economically inefficient to disperse ACEG token for open circulation prior to establishing the meta-voting technical and operational infrastructure. For this reason, the token may exist prior to the on-chain TGE in the form of the non-transferable stACEG and sdACEG voting derivatives. The milestones include:

1) the early strategic supporters funding round, founding of the global DAO ACER treasury;  
2) initial distribution of the privately secured ACEG into the voting stake and security deposit, deployment and release of stACEG and sdACEG;  
3) launch of the regional liquidity pools, commencement of the DAOs operation;  
4) transition towards the secure ACER and ACE\[cc\] token implementations;   
5) ACEG token generation event and optional public IDO, start of the on-chain vesting schedule;  
6) launch of the internal ACEG/ACER pool and the associated infrastructure.

**ACEG Token metrics**

The following TGE distribution shares and vesting schedules are currently offered:

Maximum supply \= 1 billion ACEG  
Network valuation \= USD 100 million  
Implied price \= USD 0.1 per ACEG token

Project founders: 20% of supply (200 million ACEG), 2-year lock-up followed by linear vesting over 3 years;  
Core team and advisors: 15% of supply (150 million ACEG), 1-year lock-up followed by linear vesting over 3 years;  
Supporters: 15% of supply (150 million ACEG), vesting schedule depending on the raise round;  
DAO reserve: 30% of supply (300 million ACEG), subject to the global DAO control;  
Liquidity: 20% of supply (200 million ACEG), 100 million released at TGE, the rest locked up for 1 year.
